       Proof.                                                
         We have previously seen (Theorem IV.2.2) that the map ∇ from L2(Ω)
       into (H−1(Ω))d has a closed range and thus is a Banach space. Let N be
       the kernel of this map; then we know that the map ∇ can be considered
       as a continuous linear bijection of L2(Ω)/N on ∇(L2(Ω)). From the open
       mapping theorem (Theorem II.2.3) we know, therefore, that ∇ produces an
       isomorphism of Banach spaces between L2(Ω)/N and ∇(L2(Ω)).
